items.q: Why are you shy in the first place?
items.a: Because you've **practiced being shy** so long you're expert at it. Confidence also takes practice. Shyness is **self-centric thinking** — *"I'm not interesting / funny / smart enough"* is all **me me me** inward focus.

items.q: Is the jump from shy to confident one leap?
items.a: No. The middle step is **not looking shy** and **not sounding shy** — behaviors others read as confidence even when you still feel nervous. That **perceived-confidence loop** then rewires how you see yourself.

items.q: What visual habits make you look less shy?
items.a: The visual trio: **posture**, **open body language**, and **good eye contact**. Vinh's early stage hack — black shirt + vest to hide sweat — still earned *"you seemed so confident"* feedback that started shifting self-image.

items.q: What vocal habits stop you from sounding shy?
items.a: Volume at least **5–6/10** (not 3), **end sentences on lower pitch** (avoid uptalk), and **pause more**. Those three read as composure even before you feel it.

items.q: How does a curious mindset reduce shyness in conversation?
items.a: When they mention archery, ask **how they got in**, **what sparked passion**, **hardest part**, heroes — about **three follow-ups**. Outward questions break the self-centric spiral.

items.q: What should you do instead of one-word answers?
items.a: Use **elaborate replies**. "How was your weekend?" → don't stop at *"awesome"*; share **what you actually did** so others have something to connect with.

items.q: What is the fastest rapport builder Vinh recommends?
items.a: A **story bank** — document daily things that happen so you always have material. A student demo (*chaco-sandals / "shoes saved my life"*) showed a clear **before/after** confidence lift from applying the tips.

items.q: What identity trap keeps shy people stuck?
items.a: Don't stay so attached to **present-you** that you deny **future-you** a chance. Transformation takes time — cling to current identity and you block practice.
